snip.t: | Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) | Is eosinophilic airway inflammation present? | Elevated FeNO (>35 ppb) suggests Th2‑high asthma and predicts steroid responsiveness |

qs.q: A clinician reviewing diagnostic biomarkers for a patient with suspected asthma notes a raised FeNO level of 55 ppb. What specific pathological process does this elevated fraction of exhaled nitric oxide reflect?
qs.e: A raised FeNO level greater than 40-50 ppb supports eosinophilic inflammation in asthma phenotypes. It does not measure fixed fibrosis or bacterial bronchitis.
